Key Research Thinking Patterns: Quantum Confinement: The researcher employs quantum confinement to enhance the performance of thermophotovoltaic devices by designing and modeling IV-VI semiconductor multiple quantum well (MQW) materials, which remove L-valley degeneracy and increase the open circuit voltage.

Optimization of Junction Layers: The researcher optimizes junction layers in thermophotovoltaic devices to achieve high power conversion efficiencies, as demonstrated in the use of Pb0.81Sn0.19Se and Pb0.8Sr0.2Se materials.

Biological and Chemical Analysis: The researcher applies mid-IR laser absorption spectroscopy to measure acetaldehyde concentrations in cell culture media samples, providing insights into cancer cell behavior and proliferation.

Materials Science and Engineering: The researcher leverages molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) and other techniques to fabricate and characterize IV-VI semiconductor materials and devices, enabling low-cost thermophotovoltaic device manufacturing.
Summary Description: Patrick McCann is a researcher specializing in thermophotovoltaics, semiconductor materials, and energy storage. His work focuses on designing and optimizing IV-VI semiconductor materials and devices for high-performance thermophotovoltaic applications, as well as developing novel methods for cancer detection and research. He employs a range of techniques, including molecular beam epitaxy, quantum confinement, and mid-IR laser absorption spectroscopy, to advance the field of thermophotovoltaics and biotechnology.
